label: conj:borromean-baryon-mass-formula
title: Borromean baryon mass formula with common Borromean term $\mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0)$
html:
Conjecture. Borromean baryon mass formula with common Borromean term \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0)

Conjecture (Borromean baryon mass formula, common-scale form). Every Borromean baryon B = \mathcal{B}_3(K_{0_1}, K_{0_1}, K_{0_1}) \oplus \mathcal{L}_H has rest mass:

  \mathfrak{m}(B)
  \;=\;
  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0)
  \;+\;
  m_e \cdot S(B)

where m_e is the electron mass, S(B) is the Skein contribution of the orientation partition evaluated at q_0, and \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0) is a common Borromean term depending only on the Borromean complement \mathcal{B}_3 (with \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \approx 7.327) and q_0 — shared by all Borromean baryons.

The common-scale hypothesis asserts that \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0) ignores the internal orientation partition: the orientation dependence falls entirely on the Skein term S(B). The difference \mathfrak{m}(n) - \mathfrak{m}(p) is then independent of the common term. The resulting prediction matches the beta-decay residual to within 1015 ppm. The canonical absolute normalisation of the common term is the muon-anchored Hecke energy of computations/canonical_mass.py; only the orientation-independent cancellation, not any particular closed form for \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0), is used here.
